title: Killer baseline
text: Killer baseline The creator accepts this as a useful working foundation. Fine tuning is deliberately paused while game and environment design improve. Do not mistake that decision for final AI or difficulty acceptance. Sensing and search tuning Killer Walk hearing Run hearing Search budget Search points Groundskeeper 10 m 20 m 18 s 4 Rattletrap 14 m 26 m 22 s 5 Roadkill 8 m 18 m 14 s 3 Hitchhiker 8 m 16 m 12 s 3 Usher 9 m 18 m 18 s 4 Switchboard 10 m 22 m 20 s 4 Movement sensing uses horizontal player speed: greater than 0.6 m/s starts walking noise, greater than 3 m/s uses running range. Detection distance is spherical. Soft Soles multiplies movement ranges by 0.75. Safe, downed/ineligible, and suspended players are excluded. This does not inspect microphone input. Visible and audible candidates are distinct. Vision takes priority; sound behind cover starts investigation without granting sight-only warnings/attacks. New sound evidence refreshes at most every 0.8 seconds. When a player becomes quiet or leaves hearing range, the last evidence and deadline stop following them. Rattletrap remains blind, with the largest movement ranges and separate task-noise investigation. Usher investigates after a broken warning and must warn afresh when it visually reacquires. Turning corners and searching Observed movement can project a short continuation, bounded to five metres. Mode 6 searches alternate nearby reachable NavMesh probes with authored route anchors. Missing route anchors no longer cause instant abandonment. Searches have both time and point budgets, so the configured duration is a ceiling rather than a guaranteed wait. Search pauses sweep left/right for 2.2 seconds through a ±100° range. Moving patrol/search adds bounded lateral scanning (±28° patrol, ±45° search) without stopping navigation. Actual facing drives vision and presentation. Synced checkpoint fields preserve probe position, progress, reference heading, and sensing state. The hearing pass did not increase speeds. The baseline uses roughly 3.25 m/s pursuit, 3.1 for Rattletrap and 3.65 for a Hitchhiker burst; player walk/run are 2.7/4.3 before modifiers. There is no claim that these values produce fair pressure for every party size. Presentation and debug surfaces The world killer model and spectator map use the same always-active feed. Non-owners wait for a matching pose, snap on the first valid sample/round change, then interpolate nearby updates. Feed data includes warning/hazard/decoy state and hearing ranges. The map’s gold vision outline is clipped against cover; blue rings show walking/running hearing. Explicit sorting keeps them above terrain. Only eligible dispatch spectators can view tracking. The map is a horizontal projection, so vertical cover and actual head visibility can differ. Host → AI diagnostics is an optional independent reader for owner IDs, heartbeat age, path state, feed receipt, presentation readiness, and movement information. Radar visibility and diagnostics are development features; decide whether to remove or restrict them before release. Deferred work and acceptance Fair search persistence and pressure distribution for solo through 16 participants. Human evasion across multiple corners, noisy work, decoys, and changing routes. Roadkill charge visibility versus actual hits under latency. Hitchhiker warp presentation and safe relocation tells. Switchboard hazard cover rules, warning/active distinction, and alternate escape routes. Unreachable targets with reachable alternatives and owner changes in every mode. Cooldown/stun immunity and strong-perk builds without unavoidable chains. The local lanes cover navigation, frozen evidence, hearing boundaries/perks, search expiry, synced metadata, and rendered rings/cones. The fresh uploaded fairness and migration matrix remains open.

title: Environment & art direction
text: Environment & art direction The current worlds are functional grayboxes with original placeholder geometry and synthesized sounds. The next pass should make the trip worth playing repeatedly before investing in fine AI tuning. Campfire as a gameplay anchor The protective lantern and covered van refuge are the dependable destination in every stop. Make their warm silhouette readable from escape routes. Preserve generous access and standing room for the crew; do not turn the entrance into a narrow collision trap. The van body is currently solid and the protected play space is its covered exterior. A walkable interior is an art/layout decision still to make. Keep exterior capacity even if an interior is added. Two locations to develop Area Existing foundation Next design questions Camp Deadwood Cabin/shed/shelter shapes and wooded routes Which loops create a second escape option? Where can the van lantern be glimpsed? Which shelters allow readable corner searches? Last Chance Service Station Pumps, canopy/garage/store and vehicle cover How do open forecourt risk and close service corridors differ? Can every job be approached from more than one direction? Aim for roughly 15–25 seconds of travel from the van to ordinary work sites. This is a design target to measure, not a claim that every current route meets it. Compact solo routes should remain interesting; larger crews need additional useful work sites, not just more repeated walking. Objective and round design Make cargo destinations, repair states, shared supplies, and extraction unmistakable through shape and feedback, not color alone. Retain interrupted repair progress and a soloable path through every mandatory task. Give leaving the refuge a reason: visible jobs, optional supplies, and short risk/reward decisions. Measure the 20/150/30/10-second phase rhythm with real players before changing timers. Test whether three stops produce variety through placement and killer combinations rather than repetitive chores. Preserve at least two plausible responses to ordinary pursuit; avoid compulsory dead ends and unavoidable spawn attacks. Art sessions 1 — Van and campfire: distressed company paint, protective lantern, awning, broad access, warm safe silhouette. Preserve zone, arrival, interaction, and navigation transforms. 2 — Killer identities: six strong silhouettes on a shared modest rig foundation. Keep visual weapon reach consistent with the simulation. Current procedural limb animation expects named arms/boots; replace deliberately if adding Animator rigs. Preserve attack warnings and hazard readability. 3 — Environment and sound: a modular cabin/garage kit, canopy, low-poly trees, shared atlas, and clear objective props. Replace synthesized warnings and decoy clicks with short original sounds; add restrained ambience and fire. Check voice-chat intelligibility and phone speakers. Asset budgets and authoring guardrails Current recorded geometry is 46,438 triangles across all loaded meshes . Initial mobile targets are below 70 MB download and about 250,000 visible world triangles; these are provisional, not frame-rate evidence. Start with a shared 1024-pixel atlas and simple materials. Prefer baked lighting, few transparent layers, limited particles/rigs/physics, and pooled supplies. There are 24 authored supply anchors per area; preserve compact solo eligibility and distinct reachable locations. Do not move protected zones, objective anchors, supply anchors, killer spawn points, or patrol routes accidentally when replacing meshes. Structural changes require navigation/lighting rebakes, scene validation, and all three platform builds. Add authors/licenses to credits when importing outside assets.

title: Development status

The creator reports that the basic game works, killers now provide a useful baseline, and Pass Host plus AFK Claim Host have been tested. The next priority is game and environment design; fine AI tuning is deferred until those decisions are clearer. These notes are unlisted, public documentation . The seven latest local lanes contain 855 passing assertions , spanning structural checks and explicit single-VM fixtures. That is useful regression evidence, not 855 real multiplayer scenarios. See testing and release gates for exact lanes, dates, build sizes, and limits. Design work comes next Establish the rhythm of a stop: safe planning, uncertain search, readable pursuit, escape, and a short breather. Redesign the two graybox layouts around that rhythm, especially solo routes and the approach to the refuge. Define the van/campfire and six killer silhouettes before investing in detailed props. Play the core objectives repeatedly with small and large groups before changing AI numbers again. Keep regression coverage and record every new uploaded test with build, devices, party size, and result. Detailed systems , AI , environment/art , roadmap , and publishing instructions are maintained separately.

title: Updating this site
text: Updating this site One normal project push The canonical website source lives at Docs/site/ in the main SpookCo repository. Edit the Markdown in Docs/site/content/ , commit it with the rest of the project, and push main . The Publish documentation GitHub Action builds and checks the site, then copies only the generated website into the separate kittynXR/spookco-docs repository. GitHub Pages serves that repository at spookco.kittyn.cat . There is an ignored local checkout at Docs/site-repo/ for inspecting the deployment repository. It is not a submodule and does not need to be committed from the game repo. Do not author content there: the next publish replaces generated pages. No Unity assets, client logs, player data, or game source are copied to the public docs repository. Editing map File or folder Purpose content/index.md Player landing-page copy content/guide/ Quick start, controls, equipment, progression, threats, FAQ content/internal/ Current status, systems, AI, art/design, roadmap, testing, publishing assets/site.css Shared responsive visual design assets/site.js Navigation/search enhancement assets/night-shift.svg Original decorative illustration, not a screenshot build.py Markdown rendering, templates, separate search indexes, sitemap check.py Broken links/anchors and public/internal separation checks requirements.txt Pinned Markdown dependency The existing engineering reports outside Docs/site/ remain project documentation. They are not blindly mirrored to the public site. Update the curated status/testing pages when a new result supersedes an older one. Label results as implemented, locally checked, user confirmed, or open; include the tested build and date when available. Preview locally From Docs/site/ , create a Python 3.12+ virtual environment, install requirements, then run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python build.py python check.py python -m http.server 8765 --directory _build --bind 127.0.0.1 Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and /internal/ . The build output and local environment are ignored by Git. The Action uses the same build/check commands before publication. Publishing and credentials The publishing Action runs for changes under Docs/site/** or its workflow, and can be run manually. It has read-only access to the main repo and uses a dedicated SSH deploy key with write access only to the docs repository. The private key is stored in the main repo’s SPOOKCO_DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY Actions secret. Never put its contents into source, Markdown, or logs. SSH host verification uses GitHub’s pinned Ed25519 host key. The docs repository publishes generated files from main at the repository root, with a .nojekyll file and CNAME containing spookco.kittyn.cat . Each deployment records the source revision in build-info.json . A failed build/check stops before replacing the deployed site; pushes are normal fast-forward updates with no force push. If publication fails, inspect the main repo’s Action first, then the docs repo’s Pages build/deployment. Confirm the deploy key still exists and the custom domain points to GitHub Pages. Cloudflare proxy/certificate changes can affect HTTPS independently of a successful site build. Public versus internal Player pages, player navigation, the public search index, and sitemap contain no links to /internal/ . Internal pages have their own navigation/search and noindex, nofollow metadata. This is discoverability separation, not authentication . Someone with the URL can read or share the pages, and the generated docs repository is public. Do not publish secrets or sensitive operational details here. If actual private team documentation becomes necessary, put it behind authentication instead of relying on an unlisted path. Platform references Publishing follows GitHub’s Pages publishing-source documentation , custom-domain setup , and deploy-key documentation .

title: Roadmap & open decisions
text: Roadmap & open decisions The original two-week plan remains a delivery framework. The current implementation moved ahead of final content, but not all acceptance gates are closed. The next pass prioritizes game and environment design while preserving the working killer baseline. Next: make the stops distinct Review solo and group routes in both areas and the readability of safe refuge access. Define the van/campfire visual identity and decide whether the van needs a walkable interior. Improve objective feedback and meaningful scavenging decisions. Choose a cohesive palette, lighting mood, modular environment kit, and six killer silhouettes. Measure short-loop fun and pacing with ordinary players before further AI tuning. Then: finish integration and scale Implement the accepted 18-person instance overflow policy while keeping gameplay tuned for 1–16 participants. Complete actual concurrent loot/purchase/cargo tests and reconnect A → B → A testing. Exercise ready countdown races, late entry, withdrawal, and quota reductions. Extend host-control testing beyond the user-confirmed Pass Host/AFK claim path to departures, cancellation, and suspension. Verify VR wrist/floating inventory, touch ergonomics, desktop direct shortcuts, and all accessibility alternatives. Then: balance, content freeze, and profiling Tune rewards toward a meaningful upgrade around the first half-hour and 20+ hours to full perk capacity; neither timing is yet measured. Test all six killers with starter solo loadouts in both areas and with larger groups. Review charge/warp/hazard fairness, repeated stuns, and strong perk combinations. Complete art/audio, warning clarity, credits, dawn report polish, and the final status of spectator radar/AI diagnostics. Run 30-minute 1/16-player performance sessions, report world and public-avatar costs separately, and fix measured bottlenecks. Release targets The working plan targets a September 27, 2026 release candidate with a buffer before the planned October 1, 2026, 11:59:59 p.m. Pacific submission deadline. These are planning dates. Recheck the official contest rules, content requirements, and submission instructions before release; this site is not an eligibility ruling. Produce matching PC, Android, and iOS builds, review SDK warnings and credits, upload manually, and submit manually. Do not equate successful asset-bundle compilation with a released world or contest submission. Decisions still open Decision Why it matters 18-person overflow behavior Creator exceptions can exceed a 16-person instance cap; runtime admission still needs handling. Final spectator information Full sensing radar may undermine mystery; current display is useful for testing. Debug controls in release Determine whether to strip, gate, or retain diagnostics. Van interior versus exterior refuge Changes art effort, collision, capacity, and navigation. Solo/group pressure and economy Current numbers are initial tuning; measure fun and progression. Final art/audio scope Keep two areas and six identities achievable without increasing mobile cost excessively.

title: Systems & architecture
text: Systems & architecture The game-host role and simulation ownership are independent. Passing Host changes who can operate the lobby/round controls; the simulation owner keeps advancing gameplay without waiting for host input. Runtime boundaries Component Responsibility SpookRules Stable catalogue IDs, tuning, XP curve, pouch packing, quota and movement rules SpookSession Phases, deadlines, crew state, host offers/claims, health/recovery, trip choices SpookLedger Inventory/shop transactions, loot manifests and claims, rewards, cooldowns SpookProfile Restoration gate, permanent profile, bounded session wallets, accepted revision saves SpookObjectives Cargo reservation/carry/delivery, retained repairs, rescue work SpookKiller One native NavMesh agent, sensing, evidence/search, attacks, durable AI checkpoint SpookMapFeed Always-active shared killer/crew tracking and remote presentation snapshot SpookSpectatorMap Local spectator map, vision/hearing presentation and tracking age SpookControls Unified action routing, input priorities, saved device profiles SpookLoot At most 12 pooled shared supply objects; no per-pickup Update SpookPanel / SpookFeedback Throttled UI, markers, interaction targets, alerts SpookTransition Local fade/teleport sequencing and replacement of obsolete destinations Authority and transactions Network entry points validate the actual caller, eligibility, and relevant revisions. A local click never grants an item. The ledger owner commits pouch changes and the shared claim in one synchronized object, with claimant/grant identity and duplicate protection. Full capacity rejects collection without claiming the pickup. Loot is rolled once per trip/stop. Restart Current Stop reuses the area, killer, manifest, and claims. Reset Trip rewinds flow while retaining cached history. Normal trip completion allows new rolls. Objective and result reward masks prevent repeated reset awards; once-per-stop abilities and equipment cooldowns are also preserved. Initial quotas and loot counts use the participating-player snapshot. Joins do not increase active quotas or supplies. Departures, withdrawal, and sustained suspension may lower outstanding requirements without erasing finished work. If nobody remains active, return to the lobby without completion rewards. Persistence Wait for OnPlayerRestored before writes, purchases, and grants. The permanent profile holds XP, survival points, perk selection, reusable gear, and player identity token. Separate VR/desktop/touch keys hold controls. A synchronized random live-session key survives trips, resets, role changes, and ordinary ownership migration. A bounded 128-record history stores session cash, pouch, cooldowns, inventory revisions, grant identity, and reward masks. The current wallet is updated during play; the history index changes only on session entry/eviction. Old prototype wallet data has a migration path. The implemented goal is same-session rejoin and A → B → A restoration without duplicated loot or refunded consumption. Actual cloud timing, interrupted writes, and concurrent-client race behavior remain uploaded acceptance work. No departure callback can guarantee a final cloud write after an abrupt crash. Stable content IDs Areas: 0 Camp Deadwood, 1 Last Chance Service Station. Killers: 0 Groundskeeper, 1 Rattletrap, 2 Roadkill, 3 Hitchhiker, 4 Usher, 5 Switchboard. Consumables: 0 empty, 1 ration, 2 soda, 3 flare, 4 tape. Reusable gear: 0 decoy, 1 camera, 2 EMF pager, 3 track shoes. Perk bits: Spotter, Courier, Mechanic, Field Medic, Scrapper, Soft Soles, Adrenaline, Quickdraw, Hardhat, Second Wind. Preserve IDs when replacing art or changing display names. Three consumable slots use three bits each and allow duplicates. XP to the next level is 150 + 35 × (current level − 1) through level 40; 31,785 total XP. Final reward pacing has not been measured. Capacity and transport limits Runtime admission is still 16 despite several storage/feed arrays having 32 slots. The accepted 18-person overflow requirement is not complete just because arrays are larger . Define admission, participants, and spectators explicitly before changing the cap. The AI checkpoint and presentation stream are separate. The always-active manual feed requests updates at 4 Hz; matching trip/stop/area/revision is required. A new owner can recover from a fresher presentation pose under a recovery interval. Local decoding/interpolation tests do not prove Photon delivery or suspension recovery.

title: Testing & release gates
text: Testing & release gates Evidence cutoff: September 13, 2026 Pacific (build/test timestamps below use September 14 UTC). No new game-code changes were made for the website. The baseline was built and tested before its checkpoint commit. Human reports The creator reports that the basic loop works and the current killers are a useful baseline. Pass Host and AFK timeout / Claim Host have been tested in uploaded play. Desktop and iPhone have been tried. Earlier reports drove fixes for stalled pursuit, non-owner registration/tracking, desktop pointer/menu behavior, and sensing-outline visibility. These reports do not close every killer, device, and networking case. The held-W issue was attributed by the creator to the KVM setup and does not occur with the physical keyboard; no game-side keyboard workaround is required for that report. Hardware and performance Available: Linux PCVR with RTX 3090; Windows AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700; Quest 3; iPhone 16 Pro. Other testers can cover standalone Android phones. Confirm the exact PC headset and refresh rate when scheduling performance acceptance. Run 30-minute sessions with one and sixteen controlled lightweight avatars. Targets: PCVR 90 FPS, Quest 3 72 FPS, iPhone 16 Pro 60 FPS . Capture CPU/Udon and GPU frame time, batches, memory, textures/lightmaps, and bundle/download cost. Report public-avatar overhead separately. No current count or build result certifies these targets. Local commands Use the existing Unity editor and fixed-command bridge; do not launch a second editor for the same project. Tools/SpookCo.ps1 exposes status , compile , validate , clientsim , stop , hearing , ai-review , replica , remote-map , map-clock , extended , and platform build commands. Use a fresh ClientSim run per test lane. An asynchronous command acknowledgment is not completion: require a fresh result log ending in SUCCESS. Do not modify scripts during a build/test. World uploads and contest submission remain manual.
